column1: # .github/ledger-secrets.tsv — every job workflow, and whether anything proves
# A job's ledger is everything about it that outlives it: the spec, every
# step's result and error, every job event, and the process log. All four are
# readable by anyone who can read a job, they are copied into backups, and none
# of them is a place a credential can be withdrawn from once it has landed. A
# passphrase-wrapped key counts as a secret; wrapping makes it attackable
# The assertion itself lives in each workflow's own package, where the harness
# that can run that workflow is. This file is the part no package can see:
# whether every workflow has one. api/internal/ledgertest's register test holds
# it to the tree, so a workflow added tomorrow fails until someone has written
# down which of the three answers applies.
#   covered    `test` names the test(s) that run the workflow on the real
#              Runner and JOBS stream and scan all four surfaces. The gate
#              fails if a named test does not exist.
#   pending    no assertion yet. `cite` names the issue that will add it, and
#              `test` is empty. This is a gap, recorded — not a pass.
#   no-secret  the workflow handles no credential material. `note` says why.
#              That claim IS the assertion for this workflow, so it is written
#              down or it is not made.

column6: The spec is a node id and the result is a round-trip time. Nothing on this path reads a credential, writes one, or asks the agent for one.
The spec is a node id and a reason string typed by the operator. The command carries no credential, and the agent needs none beyond the bus session it already holds.
